title: Consumption bands, soft-throttle and auto-overage billing acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Patel
description: PRD for implementing consumption-band pricing and a soft-throttle layer that prevents sharp service interruption while preserving predictable billing. This work defines how customers progress through discrete consumption bands (price breaks), how a short-term soft-throttle buffer is applied when customers approach a band boundary, and how automatic overage charging is computed and surfaced. The goal is to reduce surprise bills, allow graceful degradation, and enable billing reconciliation with <0.5% token-count variance.
scope: In scope: 1) Define band thresholds and pricing matrix for token and embedding consumption; 2) Implement server-side meter that assigns requests to bands in real time; 3) Soft-throttle policy (configurable percent buffer per plan) that throttles non-critical requests when nearing next band; 4) Billing calculation logic for prorated band transitions and instant overage charges; 5) UI additions in Console showing projected band progression and overage estimate; 6) Acceptance tests and billing reconciliation reports.
out_of_scope: 1) Changes to contract/legal language for enterprise invoices; 2) Custom billing integrations (SaaS billing vendors) beyond CSV export and existing invoices; 3) Dedicated capacity committed pricing — that remains on reserved contract logic.
decisions: Decided to use discrete consumption bands (rather than continuous volume discounts) to simplify real-time routing and UI. Soft-throttle will operate as a lightweight token-categorization filter that defers non-interactive requests for up to 3s rather than hard 429s. Overage is charged immediately at the next band's rate and appears as a provisional line-item until end-of-cycle reconciliation (rollback window: 72 hours).
acceptance_criteria: Billing math: Monthly invoice must match meter within 0.5% for token counts and within 1% for embeddings across a sample of 500 accounts (end-to-end reconciliation test).

Band behavior: When an account crosses a band boundary, subsequent requests are charged at the new band rate in real time and the Console displays the new projected monthly spend within 30 seconds of crossing.

Soft-throttle: When usage reaches >= (band_threshold - buffer%), non-critical requests are delayed up to 3s according to a backoff schedule; 95th percentile latency for interactive routes must remain within SLO after throttling is applied.
UI: Billing dashboard shows current band, projected end-of-month band, provisional overage estimate, and a timestamped audit trail of band changes and provisional charges.

Provisional charge lifecycle: Provisional overage lines appear immediately and are marked provisional; they are automatically reconciled (confirmed/rolled back) within 72 hours after final meter aggregation. Reconciliation decisions are logged and visible in Console.

Failover: If meter service is unavailable, requests are routed to a fallback conservative-charge mode (uses previous-day averaged rate) and incidents are created; no double-billing must occur post-recovery.

Rate-limit fallback model routing: When soft-throttle is active and request is eligible for cheaper model variants, runtime routing should attempt downgrade once before throttling. This behavior must be documented and covered by integration tests.

Auditability: Every band transition and charge event exposed via the Billing API contains: timestamp, previous_band, new_band, metric_snapshot (token_count, embedding_count), triggering_request_id (if any).
Feature flags: All server-side behavior must be behind a toggle so we can rollout to 5% of accounts, then 25%, then 100% as a staged release. Toggle state must be queryable via admin Console.
test_plan: End-to-end reconciliation test across 500 synthetic tenants with varying traffic shapes (burst, steady, ramp) comparing meter vs invoice; target variance <0.5%.
Chaos test: Force meter-service latency and failure modes, verify fallback conservative-charge mode, no double-billing post-recovery.
Load test: Validate soft-throttle behavior under 10x normal QPS for sample routes and confirm SLOs for interactive traffic.
UI test: Visual validation for projected spend widget and audit trail entries on band transitions across desktop and mobile.
Security & audit test: Confirm billing-related audit logs are forwarded to existing audit pipeline and visible in customer-facing export.
notes: Trade-offs considered: continuous discounts would reduce step-change complexity but increase per-request compute to track fractional rates; we prioritized runtime simplicity and clear customer mental model.
Open question: whether to allow customers to opt out of soft-throttle (e.g., 'burst-safe' flag) for mission-critical accounts — default will be opt-in for safety.
Implementation hint: meter should emit compact deltas to Kafka and rely on final aggregator to compute monthly reconciliation. Keep provisional_charges separate from finalized_invoices in schema.
